title: Tomato Mozzarella Salad
summary: Rinse and dry one tomato, slice it into 1/2 inch rounds, lay them in a single layer on a platter, then top with salt, mozzarella, black pepper and Italian seasoning, finishing with a tablespoon of extra-virgin olive oil.
source: CaptainCook4D recipe text + task graph (Tomato Mozzarella Salad); mistake hints from train split

nodes.name: Slice the tomato into 1/2 inch slices
nodes.instruction_novice: On a clean cutting board, slice the tomato into even rounds about half an inch thick, like a thick coin stack.
substeps: Set the tomato on a clean cutting board, stem side to one side
Hold it steady with curled fingertips
Cut straight down through the tomato with a knife
Repeat, keeping each slice about 1/2 inch thick and even
nodes.end_state: A row of round tomato slices of roughly equal half-inch thickness lying on a clean cutting board.
nodes.view_hint: Cutting board from above, knife and slices

checks.question: Are the tomato pieces round slices rather than chunks or dice?
Are the slices roughly uniform and about 1/2 inch thick?
Is the cutting board clean with no leftover food debris?

mistakes.description: Chops the tomato into chunks instead of slicing rounds
mistakes.visual_cue: Irregular cubes or wedges on the board instead of flat rounds
mistakes.correction: Those are chunks. Cut straight across the tomato to make flat round slices instead.
mistakes.early_cue: Knife cutting a slice again crosswise

mistakes.description: Slices are too thick, about 1 inch
mistakes.visual_cue: Only two or three very fat slices from the whole tomato
mistakes.correction: Those slices are too thick. Aim for about half an inch, roughly the width of your finger.
mistakes.early_cue: Knife positioned far from the previous cut

mistakes.description: Slices are uneven in thickness
mistakes.visual_cue: Mix of thin and thick slices side by side on the board
mistakes.correction: Try to keep each slice the same thickness, about half an inch, so they cook and look even.
mistakes.early_cue: Knife angled rather than straight down

mistakes.description: Uses a soiled cutting board
mistakes.visual_cue: Visible crumbs, residue or stains on the board under the tomato
mistakes.correction: That board is dirty. Wipe it clean or grab a clean one before slicing.
mistakes.early_cue: Setting the tomato down on a board with visible debris

nodes.name: Place slices on platter in a single layer
nodes.instruction_novice: Gently lay each tomato slice flat on the platter so they sit side by side in one layer, not stacked on each other.
substeps: Get a flat platter or plate
Pick up one slice at a time
Lay it flat on the platter
Place the next slice beside it, not on top, until all are placed
nodes.end_state: Tomato slices arranged flat across the platter in one layer, none overlapping or stacked.
nodes.view_hint: Platter from above showing the whole surface

checks.question: Are all tomato slices on a platter or plate (not a lid or the cutting board)?
Are the slices in a single layer with no slice sitting on top of another?

mistakes.description: Slices are stacked in a double layer or piled up
mistakes.visual_cue: Slices overlapping or sitting on top of each other
mistakes.correction: Some slices are stacked. Spread them out so each one sits flat on the platter in a single layer.
mistakes.early_cue: Placing a slice onto one already on the platter

mistakes.description: Slices are tossed or dropped onto the platter
mistakes.visual_cue: Slices landing at random angles, folded or splashing juice
mistakes.correction: Place each slice gently with your hand rather than tossing it, so they lie flat.
mistakes.early_cue: Hand releasing the slice from above the platter

mistakes.description: Uses a lid or wrong item as the platter
mistakes.visual_cue: Slices placed on a pot lid or shallow container lid
mistakes.correction: That's a lid. Use a flat plate or platter for the salad.
mistakes.early_cue: Reaching for a lid instead of a plate

mistakes.description: Platter was already seasoned or garnished before slices were placed
mistakes.visual_cue: Salt, pepper, cheese or herbs on the bare platter before any tomato
mistakes.correction: Put the tomato slices on the platter first, then season them.
mistakes.early_cue: Shaker or cheese held over an empty platter

nodes.name: Drizzle olive oil over the platter
nodes.instruction_novice: Finish by drizzling about one tablespoon of extra-virgin olive oil in a thin stream over the whole platter.
substeps: Pick up the extra-virgin olive oil bottle
Measure about one tablespoon, or pour slowly
Move the stream across the whole platter
Set the bottle down
nodes.end_state: Glossy oil sheen over the tomatoes, cheese and seasonings across the entire platter.
nodes.view_hint: Platter from above with the oil bottle over it

checks.question: Is the bottle extra-virgin olive oil (not vegetable oil or vinegar)?
Does the whole platter have a visible oil sheen, not just one spot?
Has the oil been added after the salt, cheese, pepper and seasoning are already on?

mistakes.description: Uses vegetable oil instead of extra-virgin olive oil
mistakes.visual_cue: Pale yellow oil from a vegetable oil bottle label
mistakes.correction: That's vegetable oil. Use the extra-virgin olive oil bottle instead.
mistakes.early_cue: Hand reaching for the vegetable oil bottle

mistakes.description: Uses apple cider vinegar instead of olive oil
mistakes.visual_cue: Thin brown liquid from a vinegar bottle
mistakes.correction: That's vinegar, not oil. Put it back and drizzle extra-virgin olive oil.
mistakes.early_cue: Vinegar bottle picked up

mistakes.description: Adds only 2 teaspoons instead of 1 tablespoon
mistakes.visual_cue: Teaspoon measure used, sparse oil only on part of the platter
mistakes.correction: That's a bit short. Use a full tablespoon so the oil covers the whole platter.
mistakes.early_cue: Teaspoon-size measuring spoon picked up

mistakes.description: Oil poured in one puddle instead of drizzled across
mistakes.visual_cue: Oil pooling on one slice or in one corner of the platter
mistakes.correction: Move the bottle as you pour so the oil drizzles over all the slices.
mistakes.early_cue: Bottle held still over one spot

nodes.name: Gently dry the tomato with a towel
nodes.instruction_novice: Pat the rinsed tomato gently all over with a dry paper towel or tea towel until the skin is no longer wet.
substeps: Pick up a clean, dry paper towel or tea towel
Cup the tomato in the towel
Pat and turn until no water droplets remain
Set the dry tomato on the clean cutting board
parts: dry paper towel or tea towel
nodes.end_state: The tomato skin looks matte with no water droplets, resting on a towel or cutting board next to a used towel.
nodes.view_hint: Tomato and towel in the hands, close-up on skin

checks.question: Is the tomato being patted with a towel?
Is the towel dry (not soaked or dripping)?
Is the tomato skin free of visible water droplets?

mistakes.description: Tomato is left visibly wet / not dried completely
mistakes.visual_cue: Shiny water beads on the tomato skin after the towel is put down
mistakes.correction: There's still water on it. Give the tomato a few more pats until the skin looks dry.
mistakes.early_cue: Only a quick single dab with the towel

mistakes.description: Uses a wet or damp towel to dry the tomato
mistakes.visual_cue: Towel is darkened, limp or dripping while wiping
mistakes.correction: That towel is wet. Grab a dry paper towel so the tomato actually dries.
mistakes.early_cue: Reaching for a towel lying in the sink or a damp dish rag

mistakes.description: Rubs the tomato roughly instead of patting gently
mistakes.visual_cue: Fast scrubbing motion, tomato skin squeezed or dented
mistakes.correction: Go easy, just pat it gently so you don't bruise the tomato.

nodes.name: Season the slices with salt
nodes.instruction_novice: Sprinkle a light, even pinch of salt over the tomato slices on the platter.
substeps: Pick up the salt container
Take a pinch or shake lightly
Move your hand across the platter so every slice gets a little
Set the salt down
nodes.end_state: Fine white salt grains visible scattered across the tomato slices on the platter.
nodes.view_hint: Platter from above, close on slice surfaces

checks.question: Is the container being used labelled or recognizable as salt rather than sugar?
Are salt grains visible on the tomato slices on the platter?

mistakes.description: Uses sugar or powdered sugar instead of salt
mistakes.visual_cue: Sugar bowl or powdered-sugar container held over the platter; fine powder dusting the slices
mistakes.correction: That's sugar, not salt. Use the salt shaker for the tomatoes.
mistakes.early_cue: Hand reaching for the sugar container

mistakes.description: Seasons the slices on the cutting board instead of on the platter
mistakes.visual_cue: Salt falling onto slices still on the cutting board
mistakes.correction: Season the slices after they're on the platter, not on the cutting board.
mistakes.early_cue: Salt held over the cutting board

mistakes.description: Theatrical 'salt bae' sprinkle from high up, salt scatters off the platter
mistakes.visual_cue: Arm raised high, salt landing on the counter around the platter
mistakes.correction: Keep your hand low over the platter so the salt lands on the tomatoes, not the counter.
mistakes.early_cue: Arm raised well above shoulder height with salt

nodes.name: Sprinkle mozzarella on the tomatoes
nodes.instruction_novice: Take a handful of mozzarella cheese and sprinkle it evenly over all the tomato slices on the platter.
substeps: Pick up the mozzarella cheese
Take a small amount in your fingers
Scatter it over the slices, moving across the whole platter
Repeat until every slice has some cheese
nodes.end_state: White mozzarella pieces scattered evenly across the tomato slices covering the whole platter.
nodes.view_hint: Platter from above showing all slices

checks.question: Is the cheese white mozzarella rather than orange cheddar?
Is cheese spread across the tomato slices over the whole platter, not just one spot or the rim?

mistakes.description: Pours or dumps the cheese in one pile instead of sprinkling
mistakes.visual_cue: A single mound of cheese on one area of the platter
mistakes.correction: Don't dump it in one spot. Sprinkle the cheese with your fingers so it spreads over every slice.
mistakes.early_cue: Whole bag or container tipped over the platter

mistakes.description: Uses cheddar cheese and puts it around the rim of the platter
mistakes.visual_cue: Orange shredded cheese sitting on the platter edge rather than on the tomatoes
mistakes.correction: That's cheddar. Use the mozzarella, and put it on top of the tomatoes, not around the edge.
mistakes.early_cue: Hand reaching for orange cheese

mistakes.description: Sprinkles cheese onto the cutting board instead of the platter
mistakes.visual_cue: Cheese landing on the cutting board surface
mistakes.correction: The cheese goes on the tomato slices on the platter, not on the cutting board.
mistakes.early_cue: Cheese held over the cutting board

mistakes.description: Spills cheese onto the counter around the platter
mistakes.visual_cue: Cheese pieces scattered on the counter outside the platter edge
mistakes.correction: Keep your hand lower and over the platter so the cheese doesn't spill onto the counter.
mistakes.early_cue: Hand sprinkling from far above the platter

nodes.name: Rinse a tomato
nodes.instruction_novice: Take one regular tomato and rinse it under cool running water, rubbing the skin with your fingers.
substeps: Pick up one full-size tomato
Hold it under cool running tap water
Rub the skin all over with your fingers
Turn off the tap and hold the wet tomato over the sink
nodes.end_state: A single whole, wet, glistening full-size tomato held in hand or sitting beside the sink.
nodes.view_hint: Hands and tomato over the sink basin

checks.question: Is exactly one regular-size tomato (not cherry tomatoes) being rinsed?
Is water visibly running over the tomato skin?

mistakes.description: Uses a cherry tomato instead of a regular tomato
mistakes.visual_cue: A small, bite-size tomato in the hand instead of a palm-size one
mistakes.correction: That's a cherry tomato. Grab one regular, full-size tomato instead.
mistakes.early_cue: Hand reaching toward the cherry tomato container

mistakes.description: Uses two cherry tomatoes instead of one regular tomato
mistakes.visual_cue: Two small tomatoes being rinsed together
mistakes.correction: You need just one large tomato, not two small ones. Put those back and take one regular tomato.
mistakes.early_cue: Picking up more than one small tomato

mistakes.description: Skips rinsing and goes straight to drying or slicing
mistakes.visual_cue: Dry tomato goes directly to the towel or cutting board without water contact
mistakes.correction: Rinse the tomato under running water first, then dry it.
mistakes.early_cue: Tomato carried toward the cutting board instead of the sink

nodes.name: Season with 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
nodes.instruction_novice: Measure a quarter teaspoon of black pepper and sprinkle it evenly over the platter.
substeps: Find the 1/4 teaspoon measuring spoon
Fill it level with black pepper
Hold it over the platter
Sprinkle it evenly across all the slices
nodes.end_state: Dark pepper specks visible across the tomato and cheese on the platter, with an empty 1/4 teaspoon nearby.
nodes.view_hint: Measuring spoon in hand, then platter from above

checks.question: Is the measuring spoon the 1/4 teaspoon size?
Are black pepper specks spread across the platter?

mistakes.description: Uses 1/8 teaspoon instead of 1/4 teaspoon
mistakes.visual_cue: Smallest measuring spoon in hand, very sparse pepper on the platter
mistakes.correction: That's the 1/8 teaspoon. Use the 1/4 teaspoon so there's enough pepper.
mistakes.early_cue: Picking the smallest spoon from the set

mistakes.description: Uses 1/2 teaspoon instead of 1/4 teaspoon
mistakes.visual_cue: Larger measuring spoon heaped with pepper; heavy dark coating on slices
mistakes.correction: That's the 1/2 teaspoon, too much. Use the 1/4 teaspoon instead.
mistakes.early_cue: Picking a larger spoon from the set

mistakes.description: Spills pepper while measuring
mistakes.visual_cue: Pepper scattered on the counter around the pepper container
mistakes.correction: Measure over the pepper container or a plate so spills are caught, then level the spoon.
mistakes.early_cue: Spoon tipping while being filled

mistakes.description: Seasons before the tomato slices are on the platter or onto a lid
mistakes.visual_cue: Pepper falling on an empty plate, a lid, or the cutting board
mistakes.correction: Wait until the tomato slices are on the platter, then add the pepper over them.
mistakes.early_cue: Pepper held over an empty plate or lid

nodes.name: Garnish with Italian seasoning
nodes.instruction_novice: Sprinkle a little Italian seasoning over the whole platter as a garnish.
substeps: Pick up the Italian seasoning jar
Open the shaker lid
Shake lightly over the slices, moving across the platter
Close and set it down
nodes.end_state: Flecks of dried green herbs scattered across the tomato and cheese on the platter.

checks.question: Is the jar being used the Italian seasoning (dried green herb blend)?
Are green herb flecks visible across the platter?

mistakes.description: Garnishes the cutting board instead of the platter
mistakes.visual_cue: Herb flecks falling onto the cutting board
mistakes.correction: The seasoning goes over the slices on the platter, not the cutting board.
mistakes.early_cue: Jar held above the cutting board

mistakes.description: Garnishes before slices are placed on the platter
mistakes.visual_cue: Herbs scattered on an empty platter
mistakes.correction: Lay the tomato slices on the platter first, then garnish with the seasoning.
mistakes.early_cue: Jar held over an empty platter

mistakes.description: Seasoning dumped in one spot instead of across the platter
mistakes.visual_cue: A clump of herbs on one slice, others bare
mistakes.correction: Spread the seasoning around so every slice gets a little.
mistakes.early_cue: Jar held still in one place while shaking
